instruction: Highlight the rows of the top 3 students (by marks) in yellow background color.

metadata.explanation: Evaluator dynamically identifies the top 3 students by reading mark values from column C, then verifies those rows are highlighted yellow. Using fuzzy color matching with tolerance=30.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete semantic coverage: Evaluator correctly verifies both requirements - (1) identifies top 3 students by marks dynamically, and (2) checks those rows are highlighted yellow.
Dynamic verification logic: Metric sorts all rows by mark values (calc.py:69-71) and identifies top 3 dynamically, not using hardcoded row numbers.
Correct getter implementation: Getter extracts both highlighting data AND mark values from column C (calc.py:46-54 in getter), providing all data needed for verification.
Proper metric logic: Metric correctly identifies top 3 rows by sorting marks in descending order, then verifies those specific rows have yellow highlighting (calc.py:65-120).
Appropriate color matching: Uses fuzzy yellow detection with tolerance=30 (R,G >= 225, B <= 30), suitable for LibreOffice Calc color variations.
Sound partial credit: Calculates score as correct_cells/total_cells across 3 rows × 3 columns (B, C, D), giving appropriate partial credit.
Robust error handling: Handles edge cases including empty marks, missing data, and both dict/filepath result types for vm_file compatibility (calc.py:16-63).
Correct parameter handling: Metric correctly accesses expected.get('check_columns') directly, following the pattern for type='rule' (no .get('rules')).
Appropriate postconfig: Saves file with Ctrl+S before downloading to ensure highlighting is persisted.
Will work correctly at runtime: Logic flow is sound - getter provides marks data, metric identifies top 3, then verifies highlighting on those rows.
